h1: El Paso County Court Ticket Lawyer — El Paso, TX
intro: Traffic tickets in El Paso County are spread across the City of El Paso's municipal court, eight county Justice of the Peace offices, and the municipal courts of Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton. Attorney Robert Navar appears in all of them for a flat fee: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 everywhere else.
summaryHeading: The agency on your citation decides the court. Start there.
summary: El Paso Police Department citations go to El Paso Municipal Court, 810 E. Overland Ave. El Paso County's rule for everyone else: a citation "by an agency OTHER THAN the El Paso Police Department" goes to the JP precinct the officer noted on the ticket.
Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton police file in their own city courts, each with its own address and hours.
Our flat fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in every JP and city court. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons.
In every court: look for a dismissal first, then ask for deferred disposition or a driving safety course where the judge allows it. Hire online and we file the appearance.

sections.heading: Read the Agency Line Before You Do Anything Else
paragraphs: Every Texas citation names the agency that wrote it, and that line, not your address, decides where the case is filed. If it says El Paso Police Department, the case is at El Paso Municipal Court, the city's court of record for Class C misdemeanors issued within the city limits. If it names the El Paso County Sheriff's Office, DPS or a county constable, the case is in one of the county's Justice of the Peace precincts, and the officer writes the precinct on the ticket.

Inside the incorporated towns, city police file in the local municipal court: Horizon City Municipal Court at City Hall on Darrington Road, Socorro Municipal Court on N. Rio Vista Rd, and the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton courts. If you cannot read the agency line or lost the ticket, the free ticket and warrant lookup finds the court for you.

sections.heading: Our Flat Fee in Each El Paso County Court
paragraphs: A ticket in El Paso Municipal Court is a flat $59. A ticket in any El Paso County JP precinct, in Horizon City or Socorro Municipal Court, or in the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton courts is $69. The difference reflects the drive and the less frequent dockets, not a different defense.

Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons of $10 to $30 each. An existing warrant is $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one, recalled as part of the same engagement; see the warrants hub. Court costs and any deferral or course fee are set by the court. The consultation is free, and the fee is flat. Hire online in about two minutes.

sections.heading: How the Dockets Differ, and What Stays the Same
paragraphs: El Paso Municipal Court is a high-volume court with multiple judges and dockets Monday through Friday, and its page tells drivers who have not entered a plea by the appearance date to expect a warrant. The JP precincts are eight separate offices, each run by an elected justice of the peace with their own hours and terms for a deferral. The small city courts hold hearings on set days or keep short clerk hours, so a missed date there can take longer to repair. Those differences change the timing and the ask; they do not change the law.

In every court the goals are the same. Our traffic ticket dismissal page explains the grounds we look for: a defective citation, an officer unavailable for trial, missing proof, and compliance dismissals. Our deferred disposition and defensive driving page explains the fallbacks under art. 45A.302 and 45.0511 and why both are in the judge's discretion. A trooper ticket gets a JP-specific plan; how to fight a traffic ticket in El Paso gives the long version.

sections.heading: Pick the Right Court Page, Then Send Us the Ticket
paragraphs: If your citation says El Paso Police, start with El Paso Municipal Court. If it says Sheriff, constable or DPS, go to the Justice of the Peace courts. For Horizon City police, see Horizon City Municipal Court; for Socorro police, Socorro Municipal Court; for San Elizario, Clint, Anthony or Vinton police, the combined valley municipal courts page. Whatever the court, send us both sides of the citation, a photo of your driver's license, current proof of insurance and registration, and any letter the court has mailed you.

Robert Navar is known for traffic-ticket and warrant defense across El Paso County's courts and also assists with expungement, occupational licenses, estate planning and injury claims. Se habla español. This page is general information, not legal advice; for advice on your case, call 915-503-1600 or schedule a free consultation.

faqs.q: How do I find out which El Paso court has my ticket?
faqs.a: The agency on the citation tells you: El Paso Police means Municipal Court; Sheriff, DPS or constable means the JP precinct written on the ticket; a city police department means that city's municipal court. Lost the ticket? The free lookup finds it.

faqs.q: Why is the fee $59 in Municipal Court but $69 in the others?
faqs.a: El Paso Municipal Court is downtown and holds dockets every weekday. The JP precincts and the city courts are farther out and hear cases less often, so each case takes more time. The defense itself is the same.

faqs.q: Is deferred disposition available in every El Paso County court?
faqs.a: The statute makes it available to every justice and municipal court, but each judge decides whether to grant it and on what terms, within the 180-day cap.

faqs.q: Can a ticket from a DPS trooper on I-10 be handled without me?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. DPS tickets are filed in the JP precinct the trooper writes on the citation, and we appear there for $69.

faqs.q: What if I missed my court date in one of these courts?
faqs.a: Call the same day. A missed date can mean a warrant, a failure-to-appear charge and a hold on your DPS license renewal. We file an appearance and ask the court to recall the warrant; see traffic warrant recall.
